rules.statement: Validate a configurable setting's value when it is set, against the exact shape its consumer reads, so that a stored value can always be used and never fails at run time.
rules.why: A value the consumer can't read, such as a CSS color the theme engine can't parse, would break the surface at run time instead of being rejected when it is set.
rules.check: Look for new settings or options whose values are stored without validation, or are validated more loosely than the code that reads them. Examples: free-form CSS colors, unbounded strings, arbitrary URIs.

rules.statement: Require a tenant-supplied URI that an end-user's browser fetches from a TLS-served page (such as a logo) to be an absolute `https` URI, and reject relative or non-https values when the setting is saved.
rules.why: The browser fetches the resource from a page served over TLS, so a non-https or relative value would not load correctly or securely.
rules.check: Look for validation of tenant or client asset URIs (logo, image and similar) that accepts relative URIs, `http`, or other schemes.

rules.statement: Restrict tenant-configurable color values to hexadecimal `#rgb` or `#rrggbb` notation, and reject named or functional CSS color notations.
rules.why: Hexadecimal is the one notation every theme engine reads the same way. Theme engines disagree on named and functional notations.
rules.check: Look for color setting validators that accept named colors, rgb()/hsl() or other CSS notations, or that skip validation.

rules.statement: Bound display-name style settings to a maximum length, and reject control characters in them.
rules.why: A stored value must always render. The source limits display names to 100 characters with no control characters.
rules.check: Look for display-name or title settings that are validated without a length limit or without rejecting control characters.
